sections.heading: Section 1: Discrete Random Variables and Bernoulli Likelihood

questions.q: In a binary click-through model, an ad is clicked $k = 40$ times out of $n = 200$ impressions. What is the Maximum Likelihood Estimate $\hat{p}_{MLE}$ of the click probability?
What is the variance of a Bernoulli random variable with success probability $p = 0.3$?
Show how maximizing the Bernoulli log-likelihood relates to the binary cross-entropy loss function used in neural networks.
choices: Maximizing Bernoulli log-likelihood is mathematically identical to minimizing binary cross-entropy
Cross-entropy is the reciprocal of the log-likelihood
questions.answer: Log-likelihood is $\sum [y_i \ln p + (1-y_i)\ln(1-p)]$. Binary cross-entropy is the negative log-likelihood $-\text{LL}$.

questions.q: A feature vector component follows $X \sim \mathcal{N}(50, 16)$. What are its mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$?
By the empirical ($68-95-99.7$) rule, approximately what percentage of samples from $\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ fall within the interval $(\mu - 2\sigma, \mu + 2\sigma)$?
questions.answer: Approximately $95.4\%$ of Gaussian mass lies within $\pm 2$ standard deviations.

questions.q: Standardize the value $x = 62$ from the distribution $\mathcal{N}(50, 16)$ into a standard normal $z$-score.

sections.heading: Section 3: The Likelihood Function and Log-Likelihood Formulation

questions.q: Why is the log-likelihood $\ln L(\theta) = \sum_{i=1}^n \ln p(x_i | \theta)$ preferred over raw likelihood in machine learning optimization?
choices: It transforms products of probabilities into sums, preventing numerical underflow and simplifying derivatives
It converts non-convex problems into concave problems unconditionally
It eliminates the need for normalization
It ensures the sample mean is zero
questions.answer: Multiplying many small probabilities causes float underflow; summing logs is numerically stable and derivatives split cleanly.

questions.q: For $n$ independent samples from $\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$, what is the analytical expression for the log-likelihood?
questions.answer: Taking natural log of $\prod \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} \exp\left(-\frac{(x_i-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)$ gives this standard form.

questions.q: Given $5$ observations $\{2, 4, 4, 6, 9\}$, compute the sample mean $\bar{x}$, which is the Gaussian MLE $\hat{\mu}_{MLE}$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Properties of Estimators: Bias and Consistency

questions.q: Why is the Maximum Likelihood Estimator for variance $\hat{\sigma}_{MLE}^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2$ biased for finite samples?
choices: Its expected value is $\frac{n-1}{n}\sigma^2 < \sigma^2$, underestimating true variance due to using sample mean $\bar{x}$
It only works for standard normal data
questions.answer: Estimating $\bar{x}$ uses 1 degree of freedom, resulting in $E[\hat{\sigma}_{MLE}^2] = \frac{n-1}{n}\sigma^2$ (Bessel's correction uses $n-1$).

questions.q: What is Bessel's correction to make the sample variance estimator unbiased?
What does it mean for an estimator $\hat{\theta}_n$ to be asymptotically consistent?
choices: As sample size $n \to \infty$, $\hat{\theta}_n$ converges in probability to the true parameter $\theta$
The estimator has zero variance for all sample sizes
The estimator follows a student-$t$ distribution
questions.answer: Consistency is the property that with infinite data, the estimator converges to the ground truth parameter value.
